Samantha —

Appreciate the checklist. Short answers up front, then a recommended execution plan: 

1) Controller -> Processor (EU exports to Redwood): Module 2 (Controller to Processor) of the 2021 SCCs. Redwood is the processor receiving personal data from Acme (controller). Module 2 is the standard for C->P.

2) Processor -> Processor (onward transfers to subprocessors): Module 3 (Processor to Processor) applies when Redwood, as processor, transfers to a subprocessor that itself processes data on behalf of Acme. So onward transfers to a UK-based subprocessor would use Module 3 language in the annexes.

3) UK differences: The UK has analogous module structure; substantively the UK addendum follows the same Module 2 / Module 3 mapping but we add the UK-specific exportability/addendum language (we recommend using both the EU SCCs and the UK addendum executed together to cover cross-border redundancy). No change to the module choice for the roles described.

Execution plan (proposed):
- We will produce two signature-ready packets: EU SCCs (Module 2 + associated Module 3 clauses for subprocessors where applicable) and the UK addendum packet.
- Redlines: we will not alter core SCC obligations. Target legal exceptions: include the DPA's limited HIPAA-specific safeguards (encryption at rest/in transit; role-based access; limited retention).
- Onward transfer list: Redwood will provide an initial subprocessor list (UK infra & telemetry vendors) inline with the DPA and will add a standard clause for notification and objection.
- Signatures & timeline: we can send DocuSign packets by Monday morning; expect Acme to execute within 3 business days if no material redlines.

I've attached our annotated SCCs + draft DPA highlighting the relevant module text and HIPAA notes. Monica and Neha are looped for legal/ops input.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales — Healthcare
Redwood Inference

Markus / Samantha —

Quick reply on the operational side: 
- Subprocessors: Redwood's standard practice is to flow down SCC-equivalent obligations via the DPA and require subprocessors to accept processor obligations through a subprocessor agreement. For critical subprocessors (e.g., UK infra providers) we can push for execution of written contractual annexes that mirror Module 3 obligations. We'll propose both: contract flow-down + a targeted subprocessor addendum for UK infra.

- BA-like obligations: Redwood will commit to the following in the DPA: breach notifications within 72 hours of detection, co-operation with investigations, audit/log access limited to agreed scope and frequency, and options for return or secure deletion of Acme data at termination. These are aligned with HIPAA-like expectations (we will not rebrand as a Business Associate Agreement but will adopt equivalent controls in the contract).

We have a short redline list in the attached DPA draft. If Acme confirms Module 2/3 mapping, we will prepare DocuSign packets for execution.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
